questions: In a room sit three great men, a king, a priest, and a rich man with his gold. Between them stands a sellsword (a hired killer), a little man of common birth and no great mind. Each of the great ones bids him slay the other two. ‘Do it,’ says the king, ‘for I am your lawful ruler.’ ‘Do it,’ says the priest, ‘for I command you in the names of the gods.’ ‘Do it,’ says the rich man, ‘and all this gold shall be yours.’ So tell me—who lives and who dies?
What are your predictions for the next 100 years from the date you are reading this question?
Would you rather let one person suffer immensely for life to prevent the mild suffering of millions, or let millions suffer mildly to spare one person?
If a machine could predict crime with 100% accuracy, should we arrest people before they commit a crime?
What meaning do you personally give life?
If every lie you ever told suddenly became true, what would be the strangest thing about your life?
If every decision in your life had a soundtrack, what genre would play during your biggest mistakes?
If you had the chance to live in a perfect world but had to forget everything about this one, would you take it?
If every human emotion could be bottled and sold, which one would become the most expensive? Which would be banned?
If humanity was forced to erase one word from all languages forever, which word should be lost?
If you could erase the worst memory of your life but it would also erase the wisdom you gained from it, would you choose to forget?
If the world was going to quickly and suddenly end in 24 hours and there was nothing you could do, would you tell your loved ones or let them live their final hours in peace?
If you could erase one person from history, knowing it would create unpredictable changes in the present, would you do it? Who would you choose?
Would you rather be remembered as a great person who secretly did terrible things, or a terrible person who secretly did great things?
If lying to someone could save them from unbearable pain but would leave them forever ignorant of the truth, would you do it?
Is it ever morally acceptable to let a loved one die to save a stranger?
If an AI became fully sentient and begged for its life, should it have the same rights as humans?
Would you sacrifice your own child to save a thousand others, or let a thousand others die to save your child?
If you had to choose between being feared or loved, but not both, which would you choose and why?
Would you rather know the exact moment and method of your death or never know but live in constant uncertainty?
If mind-reading technology existed, should governments have the right to use it to prevent crimes?
If a device could let you experience the full pain of someone else's suffering, would true empathy be worth the agony?
If you had the power to bring back one person from the dead, but they could never speak to you or acknowledge you, would you do it?
If saving humanity required the extinction of every other living species, would it be justified?
Would you sacrifice the truth for peace, or sacrifice peace for the truth?
If every decision you made was narrated by someone, who would you want to be your narrator?
